result.abstractText:
Background

Severe cenesthopathy associated with major depressive disorder (MDD) may cause malnutrition and functional decline. We report three elderly women with trunk and visceral cenesthopathy associated with MDD who improved markedly following electroconvulsive therapy (ECT).

Case presentation

Case A: A woman in her 60s developed MDD while caring for her mother with dementia. Despite pharmacological treatment, trunk, limb, and oral cenesthopathy developed 6 months later, resulting in reduced food intake and physical deterioration. Symptoms improved after six ECT sessions, nearly resolved after 12, and ECT was completed after 15 sessions without recurrence. Case B: A woman in her 70s developed MDD after prolonged caregiving stress. Despite pharmacological treatment, she developed trunk and visceral cenesthopathy with organ displacement sensations, dyspnea, speech disturbance, and loss of appetite. Cenesthopathy resolved after three ECT sessions; dyspnea and speech disturbance improved after 10. ECT was completed after 13 sessions. After recurrence, a second acute ECT course followed by maintenance ECT maintained clinical stability. Case C: A woman in her 70s with longstanding MDD developed visceral and oral cenesthopathy after discontinuing antidepressants. Despite pharmacological treatment, she became unable to eat or drink. Cenesthopathy resolved after four ECT sessions, restoring oral intake. ECT was completed after eight sessions without recurrence.

Conclusion

ECT may be an effective treatment for trunk and visceral cenesthopathy associated with MDD. Early consideration of ECT may be warranted when malnutrition or physical deterioration necessitates rapid symptom control.

result.abstractText: Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) is traditionally regarded as a biochemical marker of menopause and declining ovarian function. However, emerging evidence suggests that its role may extend beyond reproductive physiology. During the menopause transition, FSH concentrations rise progressively, initially due to declining inhibin B and later to loss of ovarian estradiol and inhibin production. Evidence of FSH effects in bone, adipose tissue, the cardiovascular system and brain has raised the possibility of broader physiological actions. Higher FSH levels have been associated with bone loss and hip fracture risk, adverse cardiometabolic and vascular changes, and cognitive decline and Alzheimer's disease. Although these associations do not establish causality, they suggest that FSH may contribute to some consequences of reproductive aging rather than simply reflect ovarian failure. Experimental studies indicate that reducing FSH may benefit bone and adiposity, while preliminary clinical evidence regarding cognition remains inconclusive. Thus, FSH may represent not only a marker of menopause, but also a potential marker of risk and, ultimately, a therapeutic target.

result.abstractText:
Purpose of review

Menopause is a neurobiological transition with important implications for neurologic care. This review summarizes the physiology and hormonal changes of spontaneous menopause and its treatment as applied to cognition, epilepsy, migraine, multiple sclerosis (MS), and stroke. It aims to serve as a resource for neurologists when managing patients in this transitional life stage.

Recent findings

Hormonal shifts associated with menopause, particularly declining estrogen and fluctuating estrogen-to-progesterone ratios, influence symptoms, disease expression, and treatment across multiple neurologic conditions. Perimenopause is often associated with subjective cognitive complaints, in part attributed to hypoestrogenism, along with secondary effects from sleep disturbance, vasomotor symptoms, and mood changes. Cognitive symptoms are often transient and rarely with objective neuropsychological deficits or progression. In epilepsy, menopause-related endogenous and exogenous hormones may influence seizure susceptibility and alter antiseizure medication metabolism. Migraine may worsen during perimenopause, especially in estrogen-sensitive phenotypes, with postmenopause stabilization once hormones plateau. In MS, perimenopause and postmenopause contribute to overlapping age-related and MS-related symptoms and is a period of high clinical need with potential acceleration in disability progression despite reduced relapse rate. Ischemic stroke risk rises sharply in postmenopausal women driven by advancing age, accumulation of cardiometabolic risk, and loss of estrogen's protective effects. Oral estrogen-containing systemic menopause hormone therapy (MHT) is associated with increased thromboembolic events (including stroke), whereas transdermal regimens seem safer and are preferred at low or standard doses (≤50 mcg estradiol patch or ≤1.5 mg [or 2 pumps] per day of 0.06% estradiol gel). Timing of initiation also modulates this risk and plays a critical role with a favorable risk:benefit window when initiated in women younger than 60 years or within 10 years of menopause onset.

Summary

Neurologists should routinely consider reproductive history, menopausal stage, symptom burden, and disease risk factors when evaluating midlife and older female patients. When appropriately selected, MHT can be safely used in many neurologic populations, with nonoral routes for estrogen and nonhormonal options generally preferred. Incorporating menopausal considerations into neurologic practice offers an important opportunity to optimize care and advance precision medicine.

result.abstractText: Rapid population aging and increasing life expectancy in India, the most populous country in the world, raise questions about the quality of these added years for older adults. Cognitive impairment, in particular, is a growing public health concern in India. We estimated cognitively healthy life expectancy (CHLE) and life expectancy with mild cognitive impairment and dementia at age 60 and 70 years using life tables from the Sample Registration System and Demographic and Health Surveys, linked with cognitive health data from the Longitudinal Aging Study in India - Diagnostic Assessment of Dementia (LASI-DAD; 2017-2019). Analyses were stratified by gender, rural-urban residence, and social group (Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe [SC/ST], Other Backward Classes, and high caste). Conditional on surviving to age 60, CHLE for women was only 0.86 years higher than for men. Larger differences in CHLE between groups emerge when examined by place of residence and social group. Compared to their urban counterparts, rural women and men had 2.2 and 3.1 fewer years of CHLE, respectively. In relative terms, rural women spent 4 percentage points less of their remaining life cognitively healthy, while rural men spent 8 percentage points less. By social group, SC/ST women and men lived 3.7 and 5.3 fewer cognitively healthy years than high-caste women and men, respectively, or 5 and 12 percentage points fewer in relative terms. Decomposition analyses indicated that subgroup differences in CHLE at age 60 are driven primarily by mortality rather than differences in the prevalence of cognitive impairment.

result.abstractText:
Objective

Fertility intention among breast cancer survivors of childbearing age is influenced by clinical, personal, and social considerations. Therefore, multidimensional assessment is essential across treatment and survivorship. Although the Fertility Intention Scale (FIS) assesses fertility intention in women with breast cancer, no validated Korean version is currently available. This study aimed to translate and culturally adapt the FIS into Korean and evaluate its validity and reliability.

Methods

This validation study was conducted in two phases. The first phase involved translation and cultural adaptation of the FIS, including forward translation, expert panel review, back-translation, pre-testing, cognitive interviews, and linguistic refinement. The second phase evaluated psychometric properties using secondary data from 203 women aged 18-45 years with breast cancer. Construct validity was assessed using confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), known-group validity, and convergent validity. Reliability was evaluated using Cronbach's α and a 2-week test-retest analysis.

Results

The CFA indicated an overall acceptable, though marginal, model fit. Known-group validity was confirmed, as women planning pregnancy scored significantly higher on the Korean FIS (K-FIS) than those not planning pregnancy (t = 6.09, P < 0.001). Convergent validity was partially supported by a significant correlation between the K-FIS "social support" factor and perceived social support (r = 0.31, P < 0.001). Cronbach's α for the total scale was 0.93, and the intraclass correlation coefficient was 0.798.

Conclusions

The K-FIS showed generally acceptable preliminary evidence of reliability and validity for assessing fertility intention among Korean women with breast cancer. It may support tailored fertility interventions and counseling in oncology nursing practice.

result.abstractText:
Purpose

What drives a person towards death and what it entails to try to kill oneself is not fully understood. This study aimed to examine suicidality as a phenomenon, and to elucidate the essential meaning of being suicidal.

Methods

Applying Reflective Lifeworld Research, the phenomenon of being suicidal was explored through interviews with seven adult suicide attempt survivors (4 men, 3 women; aged 18-54) with various diagnoses. Interviews were analysed using meaning-oriented analysis.

Results

The four essential structures Fragile vitality versus inherent lethality, suicidal isolation, incentive of death and surrendering to death constitutes the essence of being suicidal. Being suicidal is a movement from everyday struggle for meaning and value in a perceived meaningless existence, into a fixed suicidal isolation marked by unbearable psychological pain, conviction of worthlessness and exclusion, paralyzing forces and cognitive-existential shutdown. The transition from thought to action is shaped in silent solitude by the incentive of death rather than will or choice. The inner drive towards death appears as a compelling, liberating, inevitable force impossible to resist on one's own.

Conclusion

This study provides deep understanding about the suicidal mind which may be used in development of assessment instruments and interventions for suicide prevention.

result.abstractText: Maladaptive eating behaviors such as emotional overeating, habitual overeating, and dysfunctional dietary restraint are important targets for prevention research. Psychological models suggest that difficulties in emotion regulation and early maladaptive schemas may contribute to dysregulated eating, yet longitudinal evidence remains limited. This study examined whether theoretically informed intervention contrasts affected maladaptive eating trajectories in young adult women. University women aged 18-35 years participated in a four-arm quasi-experimental study with assessments at baseline (T1), post-intervention (T2), and two follow-up assessments (T3 and T4). Participants were allocated by class groups to emotion regulation training (ER_only), schema-informed training (Schema_only), combined emotion regulation plus schema-informed training (ER_schema), or an active educational control condition. All programs consisted of twelve weekly 90-min group sessions. Active intervention conditions showed more favorable trajectories than the control condition on primary outcomes. The ER_schema condition showed the strongest and most sustained reductions in emotional overeating, habitual overeating, dietary restraint, total maladaptive eating, and emotion dysregulation. ER_only produced rapid improvements in emotion regulation, whereas the Schema_only condition showed slower improvements. Secondary outcomes were smaller and less consistent. These findings support emotion regulation as a modifiable process associated with maladaptive eating and suggest that integrating self-regulation skills with schema-informed education may enhance intervention durability. Findings are best interpreted as supporting complementary processes rather than intervention efficacy. These results may inform scalable prevention programs for young adult women and contribute to health psychology research on cognitive-emotional vulnerability and self-regulation.

result.abstractText:
Background

Sexual harassment is a serious public health problem, yet there is a lack of clarity on its measurement.

Objective

We set out to develop a measurement tool to capture sexual harassment in the different spheres of women's everyday lives.

Methods

We conducted 60 cognitive interviews with women in two iterations. In each iteration, we interviewed 10 young women aged 15-24 years, sampled from two public secondary schools; 20 women aged 25 years and above sampled from public spaces and workplaces. Iteration one explored five key questions involving concepts on unwelcome or unwanted touching, signals, and/or words or comments of sexual nature from the boy/man and a direct question on 'ever experiencing sexual harassment'. Only three questions were explored in iteration two with the additional layer of context.

Results

Majority of the participants were able to grasp the key concepts. However, they were likely to respond 'yes' to questions that were less descriptive and that included additional information on context where harassment happened. A very explicit question, 'ever experienced sexual harassment' appeared stigmatising and yielded fewer affirmative responses from the same individuals. Older women understood the questions earlier than adolescent girls who were more likely to ask for clarification and a repeat of the questions.

Conclusion

An optimal question for measuring sexual harassment must include the context for the behaviour and avoid stigmatising participants. We propose a comprehensive question that includes all forms of harassment and that can be adapted for measuring the practice in different populations and contexts.

Objective

To conduct a comprehensive assessment of physical, functional, emotional, cognitive, nutritional, metabolic, and sexual health in mid-aged women.

Methods

This cross-sectional study was conducted at the Universidad Espíritu Santo Clinic (UEES Clinic), Ecuador, as part of a multidisciplinary integrated health initiative. Women aged 40-60 years were recruited through social media outreach by the UEES Research Center and Clinic between 1 October 2024 and 1 October 2025. Interested participants scheduled a clinical evaluation by telephone. Assessments included laboratory tests (complete blood count, FSH, estradiol, HDL-C, triglycerides, glucose, and thyroid hormones [T3, T4]); validated surveys: Menopause Rating Scale (MRS) for climacteric symptoms and quality of life; Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale, 10-item version (CESD-10) for depressive mood; short Everyday Memory Questionnaire-Revised (EMQ-R) for cognition; and FSFI-6 for sexual function. Participants also underwent anthropometric measurements, body composition analysis, muscle strength testing, and dietary assessment.

Discussion

This methods paper describes a multidisciplinary approach for the comprehensive health evaluation of mid-aged women. It enables early identification of factors affecting quality of life and provides a replicable framework relevant to both local and broader Latin American contexts, serving as a model for similar initiatives across the region.

Objectives

To develop and validate the Menopause Impact Scale (MIS), a brief, person-centered measure of menopause-related symptom impact that is psychometrically robust across reproductive stages and suitable for digital implementation.

Study design

Three sequential online studies with women aged 21-85 years in the United States (total N = 2915). Study 1 (n = 486) evaluated a 57-item pool using exploratory factor analysis (EFA) and reliability indices. Study 2 (n = 1429) used confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) and item reduction to derive a brief scale. Study 3 (n = 1000) cross-validated the final structure and examined convergent and divergent validity, age sensitivity, and menopause etiology differences.

Main outcome measures

MIS total and subscale scores; structural fit indices; internal consistency; convergent validity with the Greene Climacteric Scale; divergent validity with the Copenhagen Burnout Inventory; age group and menopause etiology differences in symptom burden.

Results

EFA supported a seven-factor solution (Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin measure of sampling adequacy [KMO] = 0.968; root-mean-square error of approximation [RMSEA] = 0.048; Cronbach's α = 0.974). A 22-item model showed excellent fit in Study 2 (comparative fit index [CFI] = 0.970; RMSEA = 0.047; α = 0.964) and was confirmed in Study 3 (CFI = 0.977; RMSEA = 0.041; α = 0.941), capturing cognitive, self-perception, sexual/vaginal, musculoskeletal, vasomotor, sleep, and urinary domains. Convergent validity with the Greene total score was strong (r = 0.76); divergent validity with burnout was moderate (r = 0.57). MIS scores peaked in midlife (45-55 years). After age adjustment, symptom burden was highest in primary ovarian insufficiency, with the largest differences in vasomotor and genitourinary domains.

Conclusions

The MIS is a brief, multidimensional, impact-focused instrument with strong structural, convergent, and discriminant validity, supporting research, clinical, and digital applications.

Objectives

Drug treatment for overactive bladder (OAB) is changing, with an increasing share of β3-adrenoceptor agonists relative to anticholinergics, but it is not known how far this change has progressed in older people, who are most vulnerable to the risks of anticholinergics. We examined the use of these drugs in Japan by age and sex, and analyzed changes in anticholinergic burden using a large database.

Methods

We analyzed outpatient prescriptions of two β3-adrenoceptor agonists and six anticholinergics from FY2017 to FY2024, using the sex- and age-stratified tables of the NDB Open Data of Japan. Dispensed tablets were converted into patient-days, and the β3-adrenoceptor agonist share was calculated. Anticholinergic burden was measured as ACB-weighted prescription volume (patient-days multiplied by the anticholinergic cognitive burden score). Because FY2021-FY2022 was a period of nationwide generic supply disruption, FY2018 and FY2024 were used as endpoints when estimating change over time.

Results

The β3-adrenoceptor agonist share rose from 36.2% to 64.9%, but anticholinergic use fell only slightly (3.10 × 108 to 2.94 × 108 tablets; -5.0%). In FY2024, the β3-adrenoceptor agonist share was higher in men than in women in every age group, and the difference widened with age (+1.2 percentage points at 50-54 years and +14.2 at ≥ 90 years). ACB-weighted prescription volume was higher in women than in men, and the female-to-male ratio rose with age (1.1 at 65-74 years, 1.6 at 75-84 years, and 2.8 at ≥ 85 years). Between FY2018 and FY2024, prescription volume fell by about 20% at 65-74 and 75-84 years, but the fall was smallest in women aged ≥ 85 years (-11.3%).

Conclusions

The β3-adrenoceptor agonist share for OAB has continued to increase in Japan, but this change appears slower in older women, in whom anticholinergic exposure remains high.

result.abstractText:
Background

Menopausal transition significantly affects females's health and quality of life, largely driven by declining estrogen. Although pharmacological therapies remain the first-line treatment, interest in dietary interventions as accessible, nonpharmacological strategies is growing.

Objectives

This study aims to systematically evaluate the effectiveness of dietary interventions on vasomotor, psychological, and cognitive symptoms in menopausal females.

Methods

This systematic review included 15 randomized controlled trials (n = 1952 participants) conducted according to Cochrane methodology and Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines [International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews: CRD42024610754]. Databases searched included CINAHL, Cochrane, Embase, PubMed, and PsycINFO. Eligible studies included females aged 40-65 y experiencing menopause-related symptoms (or reporting relevant outcomes) and evaluated whole food-based interventions, structured dietary patterns, or energy restriction, excluding supplement-only trials. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool, and certainty of evidence was assessed using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted where appropriate.

Results

Twelve trials included postmenopausal females, 2 included peri- and postmenopausal females, 1 included all menopausal stages, and 1 did not specify status. Soy-based dietary interventions may modestly improve vasomotor and psychological symptoms; however, the certainty of evidence is very low. Dietary modification represents a feasible, low-risk approach, but larger, high-quality trials with standardized protocols and longer follow-up are required. Objective

To investigate the association of reproductive factors and their joint effects with lifestyle behaviours with cognitive decline in Chinese postmenopausal women.

Design

Community-based cohort study.

Setting

Shanghai, China.

Population or sample

We prospectively followed 1379 cognitively normal postmenopausal women aged ≥ 60 years for 1.8 years on average.

Methods

Menopausal age, menarche age, parity, age at first live birth and breastfeeding duration were assessed at baseline. Associations between reproductive factors or their joint effects with lifestyle behaviours and cognitive decline were examined using logistic regression. The additive interaction was evaluated by the relative excess risk due to interaction (RERI) and the attributable proportion due to interaction (AP).

Main outcome measures

Cognitive decline was defined as an annual decline in Mini-Mental State (MMSE) Examination score exceeding mean decline by 1.0 SD.

Results

The ORs (95% CIs) for cognitive decline were 2.55 (1.07, 6.06) for menopausal age < 46 years and 2.32 (1.11, 4.83) for menopausal age 46-50 years compared with menopausal age > 55 years. Meanwhile breastfeeding > 35 months (2.15, 1.02-4.51) and breastfeeding 24-35 months (2.31, 1.13-4.71) had higher risks of cognitive decline than breastfeeding < 12 months. Moreover, the combination of early menopause (≤ 50 years) and insufficient vegetable intake (1.84, 1.12-3.01), physical inactivity (2.11, 1.28-3.48), suboptimal sleep duration (2.15, 1.32-3.51), or an unfavourable composite lifestyle index (CLI) (1.76, 1.06-2.94) was associated with an increased risk of cognitive decline compared with the combination of late menopause (> 50 years) and each favourable lifestyle behaviour. Similarly, prolonged breastfeeding duration (> 23 months) combined with physical inactivity (2.10, 1.23-3.59), suboptimal sleep (2.11, 1.26-3.55), or an unfavourable CLI (2.16, 1.19-3.91) showed elevated risks compared with the combination of short breastfeeding duration (≤ 23 months) and each favourable lifestyle behaviour. Conclusions

Unhealthy lifestyle behaviours may exacerbate cognitive decline in women with adverse reproductive factors.

Background

Rectal prolapse is a condition most prevalent among older women that impacts daily quality of life. Current national guidelines recommend elective multidisciplinary management for rectal prolapse care. Despite these recommendations, little is known about the frequency and predisposing factors of emergent rectal prolapse admissions or their associated outcomes.

Objective

To quantify emergent admission rates among people with rectal prolapse, compare outcomes of emergent v. elective admissions, and identify factors associated with emergent admission.

Design

Retrospective cohort analysis.

Settings

Nationwide inpatient Sample, 2017 to 20.

Patients

Adults aged 18 years and older admitted with a diagnosis of rectal prolapse.

Main outcome measures

Primary exposure was admission type (emergent vs elective). Primary outcomes included length of stay, in-hospital mortality, and discharge disposition. Secondary outcomes included performance of rectal prolapse repair and operative approach.

Results

A total of 7,555 adult patients were admitted with a diagnosis of rectal prolapse. Of these, 1,681 (22.2%) admissions were emergent. Emergent admissions were associated with longer length of stay, higher in-hospital mortality, lower likelihood of discharge home, and greater need for postacute care. Surgical intervention was less common among emergent admissions, and perineal procedures were more common. On multivariable analysis, older age, Black and Hispanic race, Medicare, Medicaid and self-pay status, homelessness, lower neighborhood income, schizophrenia, substance use disorder, eating disorder, dementia, intellectual disability, and higher comorbidity burden were independently associated with emergent admission. Female sex and depression were associated with lower odds of emergent admission.

Limitations

The database captures inpatient hospitalizations only and diagnoses and procedures are identified using administrative billing codes.

Conclusions

Emergent admissions accounted for a substantial number of rectal prolapse hospitalizations nationally and were associated with socioeconomic vulnerability, multimorbidity, psychiatric and cognitive conditions, and worse clinical outcomes. These findings highlight existing differences in healthcare utilization for this surgical patient population. See Video Abstract.

result.abstractText: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder and is the most common form of dementia. Women are differentially affected by AD, and several sex-specific mechanisms have been explored, including hormonal differences (eg, estrogen). Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1R) are located in brain regions implicated in the pathogenesis of AD and shows preliminary evidence of modulating sex-specific pathways that may underlie differential disease risk and progression. Herein, we synthesize the extant literature on the mechanisms of GLP-1 in neurobiological systems relevant to AD pathology. Metabolic signalling (eg, GLP-1, insulin) intersects with known sex-specific pathways hypothesized to subserve AD progression in women. The preceding effects may be attributable to the disruption of estrogen signalling during the postmenopausal period, which impairs hippocampal insulin receptor function and exacerbates mitochondrial dysfunction. In addition, these mechanisms provide an explanation for AD comorbidities (eg, type 2 diabetes mellitus [T2DM]). The multidimensional effects demonstrated in GLP-1 paradigms provide a compelling rationale for further investigation of the role of metabolic signalling on sex-specific alterations in AD. Evidence across preclinical and early clinical studies suggests that GLP-1RAs may differentially influence neurobiological pathways implicated in AD pathogenesis, particularly those that interact with hormonal and metabolic systems.

Objectives

To investigate the association between adherence to the Mediterranean Diet Score (MDS) and the risk of all-cause mortality, cardiovascular disease (CVD), cancer, and dementia morbidity over 10- and 20-year follow-up periods in a population-based cohort of older adults.

Design

A prospective population-based cohort study.

Setting

Gothenburg, Sweden.

Participants

A total of 1298 participants (56.2% women) aged 70years at baseline from the general population and recruited from the Gothenburg H70 and Population Study of Women in Gothenburg (PSWG) birth cohorts.

Measurements

Dietary intake was assessed via face-to-face, semi-structured diet history interviews. The MDS was calculated based on eight food groups (excluding alcohol). Outcomes were identified through linkage with national health and death registers. Cox proportional hazard models were used, adjusting for BMI, smoking, marital status, physical activity, and education.

Results

A higher MDS was associated with a lower risk of 20-year dementia morbidity in men (multivariable-adjusted HR=0.83; 95% CI: 0.71-0.96), but not in women. This association did not remain statistically significant after correction for multiple testing, and the sex-by-MDS interaction (p=0.048) was nominally significant, but not robust to multiple testing. No statistically significant associations were found for CVD or cancer morbidity in either sex over the available follow-up (i.e., 10 and 20years, and up to 18years for cancer; 20-year CVD follow-up in men: HR=0.98; 95% CI: 0.88-1.08). For all-cause mortality, an initial association in men at 10years (HR=0.90; 95% CI: 0.82-0.99) was no longer significant after full adjustment (HR=0.92; 95% CI: 0.84-1.01).

Conclusions

Higher MDS levels were associated with lower dementia risk in men, but this finding was not robust to multiple testing correction and requires confirmation in larger studies. No association was found with all-cause mortality, CVD and cancer morbidity. A limitation of these findings is that dietary assessment was conducted at a single time point (age 70), and that dementia ascertainment relied on registers which are estimated to miss > 50% of cases, particularly among home-dwellers.

result.abstractText: Background/Objectives: Menstrual cycle tracking applications (MCTAs) are widely used digital health tools that enable women to monitor menstrual characteristics and related symptoms. However, their association with fertility health knowledge and fertility awareness remains insufficiently understood. This study aimed to examine the associations of MCTA use, duration, frequency, and purpose with fertility health knowledge and fertility awareness among women of reproductive age attending a gynecology outpatient clinic. Methods: This descriptive, cross-sectional study included 484 women aged 18-49 years who attended the gynecology outpatient clinic of a private hospital in Istanbul, Türkiye, between 1 February and 1 June 2026. Data were collected using a Descriptive Information Form, the Fertility Health Knowledge Scale (FHKS), and the Fertility Awareness Scale (FAS). Descriptive statistics, independent-samples t-tests, one-way analysis of variance, Pearson correlation analyses, and simple linear regression analyses were performed. Results: MCTA users had significantly higher FHKS total, FAS cognitive awareness, FAS bodily awareness, and FAS total scores than non-users (p < 0.001). In the regression models, MCTA use explained 8.5% of the variance in FHKS scores (F = 44.771, R2 = 0.085, p < 0.001) and 6.6% of the variance in FAS scores (F = 33.884, R2 = 0.066, p < 0.001). Application-use duration was positively correlated with FHKS (r = 0.171, p < 0.001) and FAS (r = 0.144, p = 0.001) total scores. Use frequency was also positively correlated with FHKS (r = 0.217, p < 0.001) and FAS (r = 0.119, p = 0.009) total scores. Women using MCTAs as a symptom diary had the highest FHKS scores (117.35 ± 18.78). Conclusions: MCTA use was associated with higher fertility health knowledge and fertility awareness. MCTAs may be considered as adjunctive self-monitoring tools; however, recommendations should be cautious and limited to applications with transparent, evidence-based methods and clearly communicated limitations.

Background

Menopausal symptoms significantly impair women's quality of life, and conventional menopausal hormone therapy carries risks of clinical contraindications and adverse effects. Digital health interventions (DHIs) are gaining attention as a promising non-pharmacological alternative for sustained symptom management. This study aimed to comprehensively evaluate the clinical efficacy of DHIs for peri- and postmenopausal women.

Methods

We searched 6 databases for eligible clinical studies from inception to May 2025. The methodological quality of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2. For non-randomized studies, the Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Interventions and the National Institutes of Health Quality Assessment Tool were used. The certainty of evidence for outcomes reported by RCTs was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach.

Results

A total of 8 studies involving 17,420 participants were included. DHIs utilized various mechanisms, including cognitive behavioral therapy, hypnotherapy, biofeedback-based pelvic floor muscle training, cognitive training, behavior change and self-care models, and personalized healthcare. Overall, DHIs were associated with improvements in vasomotor symptoms, psychological distress, pelvic floor dysfunction, and cognitive decline. However, there was high methodological heterogeneity and study design limitations; both RCTs were rated as having "some concerns" regarding risk of bias. According to the GRADE assessment, the certainty of evidence was low for Menopause Rating Scale (MRS) and very low for Midlife Women's Symptom Index (MSI).

Conclusion

DHIs demonstrate clinical potential as a non-pharmacological alternative for managing menopausal symptoms. Large-scale, well-designed RCTs with longer follow-up are needed. Trial registration/Protocol registration: PROSPERO (CRD420251042496).

Background

Women during the menopausal transition often experience mood disorders, sleep disturbances, and cognitive decline, making the use of psychotropic drugs relatively common. However, the relationship between psychiatric drug use and cognitive function in menopausal women remains unclear.

Methods

This was a cross-sectional study that included women aged 45-65 years from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2021-2023 cycle. Psychiatric drug use was defined based on prescription drug data, including antidepressants, benzodiazepines, and sedative-hypnotics. Cognitive function was assessed using the Digit Symbol Substitution Test (DSST). The Bayesian Kernel Machine Regression model was used to analyse the relationship between psychiatric drug use and cognitive function, with adjustment for potential confounders, including routine demographic characteristics.

Results

A total of 956 women during the menopausal transition were included in the analysis. As the number of psychotropic drugs used increased, cognitive function decline became more pronounced. Antidepressants and benzodiazepines played dominant roles in this association (posterior inclusion probability >0.9). The concurrent use of two or more psychotropic drugs was associated with an 11%-24% reduction in DSST cognitive scores. In the context of three-drug combinations, the cognitive impairment associated with antidepressants and benzodiazepines were amplified, resulting in an additional 5.1%-6.3% decrease in cognitive scores.

Conclusions

Psychiatric medication use showed a significant cross-sectional association with poorer cognitive performance among women undergoing menopausal transition, and polypharmacy regimens displayed stronger associations than single-drug regimens. Clinically, greater attention should be paid to the potential cognitive impact of psychiatric drug use in menopausal women, and polypharmacy regimens should be optimised.

Background

Menopause is a major life transition that can affect women's physical, psychological, cognitive, sexual and social well-being. Despite the availability of evidence-based interventions, many women remain insufficiently informed and experience difficulties accessing reliable information and appropriate support.

Objectives

To explore menopause-related information needs and challenges from the perspectives of menopausal women and healthcare professionals and to identify individual, healthcare-related and societal factors influencing menopause literacy.

Design

A qualitative study informed by a constructivist paradigm was conducted using semi-structured interviews and conventional qualitative content analysis.

Methods

Twenty-two peri- and postmenopausal women and 10 healthcare professionals were purposively recruited from healthcare settings in Southern Iran. Data were collected until data saturation was achieved, defined as the point at which no new codes or categories emerged from successive interviews. Interview transcripts were analysed using conventional qualitative content analysis following the approach of Graneheim and Lundman. Trustworthiness was enhanced through prolonged engagement, member checking, peer debriefing and established criteria for qualitative research.

Results

Three interrelated themes were identified: understanding and accepting menopause, menopause management, and challenges of transition. Women described menopause as an unexpected and multidimensional transition affecting physical, psychological, cognitive, sexual, social and occupational well-being. Both women and healthcare professionals identified substantial gaps in menopause literacy and emphasised the need for timely education, evidence-based information and supportive healthcare. Symptom management strategies, lifestyle modification, family and peer support, and access to reliable information were perceived as important facilitators, whereas limited awareness, menopause-related stigma, insufficient provider engagement and difficulty identifying trustworthy information were reported as major barriers.

Conclusions

Menopause literacy is shaped by interacting individual, healthcare and societal factors. Strengthening evidence-based menopause education, improving healthcare support and developing accessible, person-centred information resources may enhance women's ability to navigate the menopausal transition and inform the design of future educational and digital health interventions.

result.abstractText: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the most common type of dementia, affecting elderly women two- to threefold more than similar aged man, or the younger generations. Although 17β-estradiol offers neuroprotection, its clinical use is limited by serious side effects. This study explored a molecular group called ANGELS (Activators of Non-Genomic Estrogen-Like Signaling) as safer alternatives. A steroid library was screened via computational docking to estrogen receptor α. The top binders were preselected via in vitro and in vivo tests. The neuroprotective effect was examined in two mouse models of AD (neurotoxic and genetic). Morphological and behavioral changes were investigated. From the 15 top binders six molecules were identified without estrogen-like uterus effects and with rapid kinase activation. The chosen compound (A3270), acutely given, significantly restored cholinergic fiber loss without affecting cell loss or AD-related morphologies (amyloid β and phospho-Tau). Furthermore, it increased locomotor activity but had no effect on short term memory. These molecules lack ERE reporter activity and uterotrophic effects in vitro and in vivo and A3270 was promising in two AD model mice. We believe that these or similar compounds may provide novel approaches for AD therapy.

result.abstractText: Apathy, a transdiagnostic syndrome characterized by diminished motivation, is increasingly observed in non-clinical individuals, yet its cognitive mechanisms in non-clinical populations remain poorly understood. This study investigated the association between trait apathy and effort-based decision-making (EBDM), focusing on the critical roles of reward, probability and frame (gain vs. loss), and aimed to uncover the underlying computational processes of subjective value (SV) calculation. Participants included 84 non-clinical young adults (45 females, aged 18-25). They completed a key-pressing task where they decided to accept or reject offers that combined varying levels of effort demand, potential gain/loss frame, and probability. We analyzed behavioral measures including task accept rate and response time. Computational modeling was further employed to fit and compare different SV discounting models to participants' choices, estimating key parameters such as effort sensitivity and probability sensitivity. Compared to participants with low trait apathy, those with high trait apathy showed a significantly lower accept rate. Computational modeling indicated that this deficit was driven by the increased effort sensitivity in the gain frame and heightened probability sensitivity in the loss frame. These findings revealed that trait apathy is associated with altered effort-based decision-making, likely driven by an imbalance in how effort costs and probability-related risks are integrated into SV computation. Computational modeling provided an integrated perspective to jointly evaluate effort, reward, and probability, highlighting that apathetic individuals may require higher rewards or lower effort to act.

result.abstractText: BackgroundAnemia remains a major public health concern among adolescent girls in Ethiopia, adversely affecting physical growth, cognitive development, educational attainment, and future reproductive health. Accurate prediction of anemia severity and identification of key risk factors are essential for supporting targeted prevention and intervention strategies.ObjectiveThis study aimed to develop and compare tree-based ensemble machine learning models for multi-class prediction of anemia severity among Ethiopian adolescent girls using nationally representative survey data.MethodsThis study analyzed Ethiopian Demographic and Health Survey (EDHS) data from 2011 and 2016, including 15,952 adolescent females aged 15-19 years. Four tree-based ensemble machine learning algorithms (Random Forest, Extra Trees, CatBoost, and XGBoost) were developed and compared with a baseline Multinomial Logistic Regression model. Following TRIPOD-AI recommendations, data preprocessing included missing value imputation, categorical feature encoding, Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) for feature selection, and Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) to address class imbalance. To prevent data leakage, all preprocessing and SMOTE procedures were applied exclusively within the training folds. Models were trained using stratified 10-fold cross-validation on 70% of the data and evaluated on an independent 30% hold-out test set (n = 4786) using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and macro-average ROC-AUC. Model interpretability was assessed using global and local SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP).ResultsRandom Forest achieved the highest predictive performance, with an accuracy of 85.60% and a macro-average ROC-AUC of 94.84%, followed by Extra Trees (85.10% accuracy; 94.48% ROC-AUC) and CatBoost (83.80% accuracy; 93.08% ROC-AUC). The baseline Multinomial Logistic Regression model achieved 71.20% accuracy and an ROC-AUC of 81.50%. SHAP analysis consistently identified geographic region, altitude, educational level, household wealth index, and household size as the most influential predictors of anemia severity.ConclusionTree-based ensemble machine learning models, particularly Random Forest and Extra Trees, substantially outperformed conventional multinomial logistic regression for multi-class prediction of anemia severity among Ethiopian adolescent girls. result.abstractText:
Abstract

Testosterone is an essential endogenous hormone in women, exerting physiological actions in reproductive and non-reproductive tissues. Despite the increased demand for the use of testosterone for an array of menopausal symptoms beyond sexual functions, there is a lack of robust evidence on its impact on cardiovascular and musculoskeletal health and cognition. The aim of this review is to provide an overview of evidence-based indications of testosterone as part of menopausal hormone replacement therapy (HRT) in women and highlight the uncertainties, evidence gaps, and future research priorities. This narrative review synthesised current evidence on the physiological role of testosterone, indications for testosterone as part of HRT, clinical efficacy, formulation and prescribing, and safety profile. Testosterone declines across the adult female lifespan until the late sixth decade, and the menopausal transition itself has no meaningful independent impact on testosterone concentrations. Transdermal preparations maintaining testosterone levels in the physiological range are generally safe, with potential side effects of acne and hair growth. The existing high-quality evidence, including national and international guidelines, recommends that hypoactive sexual desire disorder (HSDD) in postmenopausal women is the only evidence-based indication for use; the evidence does not support use for any other symptom, nor for disease prevention.

Lay summary

Testosterone, widely known as the male hormone, is also produced naturally in women and plays an important role throughout their lifespan. There has been a growing use of testosterone for a range of symptoms in menopausal women, including low sexual desire, low mood, fatigue, poor memory, and heart and bone health. This review brings together the current evidence and guidelines on testosterone as part of hormone replacement therapy (HRT) in menopausal women, including its impact on reproductive and non-reproductive tissues; when it is indicated to be prescribed and in what forms; and safety and gaps in existing evidence. We found that there is high-quality evidence to support the use of testosterone for low sexual desire where conventional HRT has not helped. Transdermal preparations are recommended with no serious side effects at testosterone levels normally found in women. There is insufficient evidence to support its use for brain, heart, and bone health. This represents an area of focus for future research.

Background

Understanding how early-life reproductive timing and educational context shape cognitive aging is critical for addressing disparities in dementia risk among women. However, few studies have examined the relationship between menarcheal age and cognition in a diverse sample. This study examined associations among menarchal timing, education, and episodic memory performance in an ethnically and racially diverse sample of older women from the Health and Aging Brain Study-Health Disparities.

Methods

Using linear regression models, we assessed whether age at menarche and education were associated with performance on 2 commonly used episodic memory measures. Ethnicity-stratified sensitivity analyses and exploratory longitudinal mixed-effects models were also conducted. The sample included 780 women aged 50 years and older, racialized as non-Hispanic White, Hispanic, and Black.

Results

Earlier age at menarche and higher educational attainment were independently associated with better episodic memory performance, with more robust and consistent associations observed for Logical Memory II compared with the Spanish-English Verbal Learning Test.

Conclusion

These findings suggest that early-life reproductive timing and educational attainment are meaningfully related to episodic memory performance, with test-specific and context-sensitive patterns. Incorporating age at menarche and educational context into life-course approaches to brain health may improve the measurement of heterogeneity in cognitive aging.

Background

This study examined the effects of different exercise modalities on body composition, interleukin-6 (IL-6), and cognitive function in obese older women.

Methods

A total of 60 obese women aged ≥65 years were randomly assigned to four groups: control (CON), aerobic aquatic exercise (AAE), aerobic dance exercise (ADE), or combined aerobic and resistance exercise (AE+RE). Of these, 54 participants were included in the final analysis.

Results

Significant time-by-group interactions were observed for body weight (BW), body fat percentage (%BF), IL-6, and Korean version of the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE-K) scores. The AAE and ADE groups showed significant reductions in BW and %BF, and fat-free mass increased only in the AAE group (P<0.01). Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) increased in the AAE and ADE groups (both P<0.01), whereas IL-6 decreased in both groups (ADE, P<0.05; AAE, P<0.01). MMSE-K scores improved in all exercise groups, with scores in the AE+RE and AAE groups significantly higher than those in the CON group (P<0.001 and P<0.01, respectively).

Conclusion

Moderate-intensity aquatic and dance-based aerobic exercise over 12 weeks improved both metabolic health and cognitive function in obese older women and was accompanied by reductions in IL-6 and increases in BDNF.

Background

Insomnia is a prevalent sleep disorder associated with adverse physical, psychological, and functional outcomes. Emerging evidence suggests that vitamin D deficiency may contribute to sleep disturbances. Women are more likely to have lower serum vitamin D (25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D]) levels than men, and they also report a higher prevalence of insomnia. Although several studies have proposed that vitamin D supplementation may improve insomnia symptoms, findings remain inconsistent, and evidence from Southeast Asian populations is limited.

Objective

This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of weekly vitamin D₃ supplementation in improving insomnia symptoms, sleep quality, sleep efficiency, and functional outcomes among Malaysian women with vitamin D deficiency.

Methods

This study is a double-blind, parallel-group, randomized placebo-controlled trial conducted among women aged 19-50 years with serum 25(OH)D levels <20 ng/mL and insomnia symptoms. Participants are randomized to receive either vitamin D₃ capsules (50,000 IU/wk) or placebo (1 capsule/wk) for 9 weeks. The study is conducted in a community setting. Primary outcomes include insomnia severity assessed using the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI), sleep quality measured by the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and sleep efficiency objectively assessed using actigraphy. Secondary outcomes include daytime sleepiness measured using the Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS) and functional outcomes assessed using the Functional Outcomes of Sleep Questionnaire (FOSQ-10). Assessments are conducted at baseline, midintervention, and postintervention.

Results

Participant recruitment commenced in December 2023 and is expected to conclude in December 2026. As of July 2026, 42 participants had been screened, 33 eligible participants had been enrolled, 22 had completed the study procedures, 4 were in the intervention phase, and 1 had withdrawn due to loss of contact.

Conclusions

If the efficacy of vitamin D3 supplementation in alleviating insomnia symptoms is demonstrated, it might be proposed as a supplementary approach to cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) for insomnia. Screening for vitamin D deficiency may also be considered in individuals presenting with insomnia symptoms prior to initiating pharmacological treatment.

Design

Chronic nonspecific low back pain (CNLBP) is a leading cause of functional disability in adults. This randomized controlled trial evaluated the effectiveness of combining Cognitive Functional Therapy (CFT) with Pilates compared to Pilates alone and a control group. The primary outcome was pain intensity. Secondary outcomes included disability, fear of movement, trunk muscle endurance, and postural sway.

Setting

This single‑blind, three‑arm trial enrolled 120 women aged 20-50 years with mild to moderate CNLBP. Participants were randomly assigned to CFT+Pilates, Pilates, or control groups. Interventions were delivered over 8 weeks. Trained assessors assessed outcomes pre‑ and post‑intervention. Statistical analyses were performed using repeated‑measures ANOVA to examine group × time interactions, followed by Bonferroni post‑hoc tests for pairwise comparisons. Effect sizes were calculated using partial eta‑squared, and clinical relevance was assessed using the MCID.

Results

Significant group×time interactions were observed for pain intensity (F = 165.85, p ≤ 0.001), disability (F = 89.04, p ≤ 0.001), kinesiophobia (F = 196.48, p ≤ 0.001), and all trunk endurance and postural sway outcomes (p ≤ 0.001). Both intervention groups improved significantly compared with the control group for pain, disability, kinesiophobia, trunk endurance, and postural sway measures (p ≤ 0.001), except for total movement of the COP in the anterior-posterior direction in the Pilates group (p ≥ 0.05). However, Pilates+CFT did not differ significantly from Pilates alone for pain intensity (p = 0.871), disability (p = 1.000), or postural sway parameters (p ≥ 0.05). Significant between-group differences favoring Pilates+CFT were observed for kinesiophobia (p = 0.001), trunk flexion endurance (p = 0.003), and lateral-flexion endurance (p = 0.001).

Conclusion

Both Pilates-based interventions improved pain, disability, kinesiophobia, trunk endurance, and postural control compared with the control condition. Adding Cognitive Functional Therapy to Pilates provided additional benefits for kinesiophobia and selected trunk endurance outcomes, but not for pain, disability, or most postural sway measures. These findings should be interpreted cautiously given the mild to moderate baseline symptoms and inclusion of women aged 20-50 years.

result.abstractText: Cognitive reserve is known to support resilience against brain pathologies that affect older adults. However, the role of cognitive reserve proxies in moderating the link between post-COVID-19 cognitive dysfunction and systemic inflammation, particularly given sex differences and the potential influence of sex hormones, remains unclear. We investigated educational attainment, the most common proxy for cognitive reserve, as a moderator of the relationship between follow-up C-reactive protein (CRP) blood levels (an inflammation marker) and a composite cognitive score. Both measures were obtained during the same in-person assessment conducted between 6 and 11 months after hospitalization due to COVID-19 in a cross-sectional sample of adults stratified into four groups by sex and an age cutoff of 51 years, corresponding to the mean age of natural menopause. Regression and bootstrap analyses indicated a significant difference between women under 51 and those aged 51 or older, with higher educational attainment being associated with attenuation of the negative relationship between CRP and cognition only in women aged less than 51 years, consistent with the cognitive reserve hypothesis. Additional exploratory analyses showed a significant negative association between CRP and cognition in older men as well, but education did not moderate this association. The absence of this pattern in older women may suggest a role for sex hormones in the interplay between inflammation, cognitive reserve, and resilience. These results highlight the importance of considering sex and age-related hormonal status when evaluating post-COVID-19 cognitive outcomes.

result.abstractText:
Importance

Women in the menopause transition (MT) commonly experience mood disturbances, anxiety, cognitive complaints, and reduced quality of life (QoL). Yet access to pharmacological or psychological treatments may be limited or unsuitable for some. Identifying and accessing non-pharmacological interventions is therefore an important clinical and public health priority.

Objective

To synthesize evidence from randomized controlled trials (RCT) evaluating the effectiveness of physical activity (PA) interventions for improving depression, anxiety, mood, cognition, stress, and QoL in women during the MT.

Evidence review

A systematic search of Medline, PsycINFO, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and CINAHL was conducted from inception to April 2025. RCTs including women aged 40-65 years in peri and early postmenopause were eligible. PA interventions were compared with alternative PA or treatment as usual. Outcomes were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis, with subgroup analyses by menopausal stage (peri and early postmenopause) and intervention types (aerobic-based [ABI] and mind-body [MBI]). Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool.

Findings

Twelve RCTs involving 1,003 women were included. PA significantly improved depression (g=-1.37, 95% CI [-1.96 to -0.79], mood (g= 0.84, 95% CI [0.40-1.29]), psychological QoL (g=0.66, 95% CI [0.19-1.13]), and overall QoL (g=1.10, 95% CI [0.32-1.88]). Significant reductions in depression were found in both perimenopause (g=-1.57, 95% CI [-2.58 to -0.56]) and early postmenopause (g=-1.14, 95% CI [-1.48 to -0.79]), with other outcomes improving in early postmenopausal women. ABIs improved (g=-1.07, 95% CI [-1.35 to -0.78]), mood (g=1.05, 95% CI [0.52-1.58]), and overall QoL (g=1.41, 95% CI [0.12-2.69]), whereas MBIs improved psychological QoL (g=0.80, 95% CI [0.43-1.16]). Sensitivity analyses largely supported these findings.

Conclusions and relevance

PA may seem to improve depression, mood, and QoL in women in the MT. Both ABIs and MBIs may be beneficial, supporting the integration of PA into clinical care for menopausal women. Further high-quality trials with clearer menopause staging are needed to strengthen the evidence base.

result.abstractText:
Background

Black women in the United States face disproportionate rates of hypertension and cardiovascular disease, driven by the compounding effects of structural inequity and socially embedded stress. Social networks are a critical and underutilized lever for health promotion in Black communities. Behavioral change interventions to improve cardiovascular health are frequently delivered in group formats. Yet, it is unclear to what extent these interventions deliberately apply social network theory or measure network-level mechanisms.

Methods

We conducted a scoping review using a systematic search of 37 databases, supported by a health sciences librarian, plus a snowball search of related review articles. Studies were eligible if they targeted at least one cardiovascular health behavior, blood pressure, or a stress-reduction outcome, included a social network or social relationship measure, and enrolled samples in which at least 51% of participants identified as Black or African American.

Results

Of 524 records, eight articles representing six unique interventions met the inclusion criteria. Participants were predominantly middle-aged women from the Southern and Midwestern U.S. Social cognitive theory was the predominant theoretical framework. Network processes, including network size, cohesion, and relationship strength, were measured in half the studies and were positively associated with physical activity and weight loss outcomes.

Conclusions

The existing literature consistently underutilizes social network theory and rarely measures how network dynamics contribute to, or constrain, intervention outcomes. Future research should integrate network measurement as both a process and outcome variable and attend to the dual nature of social ties as sources of both support and strain.

result.abstractText: Cognitive symptoms are common in postmenopausal women treated for breast cancer (BC). In general and in BC, the Apolipoprotein E 4 allele (APOE4) is linked to lower cognition and accelerated cognitive decline, but exercise generally benefits cognition. The purpose of this study was to examine whether the effect of aerobic exercise on cognitive function differs by APOE4 carriage in postmenopausal women with breast cancer. Longitudinal analysis of a 6-month randomized clinical trial of aerobic exercise in postmenopausal women with BC (2016-2022) was done. Subsample with APOE genotype and cognitive function data (before randomization and at intervention completion) were analyzed. Variables included group assignment (Control/Exercise), APOE4 carriage (No/Yes), and composite scores for 7 cognitive domains (Higher = better). Robust regression was used, adjusting for age, education, baseline cognitive score, and days on endocrine therapy, with group × APOE4 carrier interaction term. In this sample (n = 116, x̅ = 62 years old, 21% APOE4 carriage), APOE4 carriage moderated the effect of aerobic exercise on learning and memory (b = -0.544, p = 0.023). Non-carriers' scores improved and APOE4 carriers' scores declined. There were no other significant findings for attention, executive function, mental flexibility, processing speed, verbal memory, or working memory. In this hypothesis-generating study, aerobic exercise was associated with modest cognitive performance improvements in non-carriers, while APOE4 carriers did not demonstrate similar improvements. These exploratory findings suggest that a differing response for effects of exercise on cognition in post-menopausal women with BC may exist and be partially explained by APOE4 carriage.

result.abstractText: Perimenopause and early postmenopause represent a critical metabolic transition with adverse changes in body composition, insulin sensitivity, lipid metabolism and cardiometabolic health, contributing to increased rates of obesity, type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease. As the prevalence of obesity continues to rise among midlife women, effective therapeutic strategies are increasingly needed. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) have emerged as highly effective treatments for obesity and type 2 diabetes through their effects on appetite regulation, weight reduction, glucose homeostasis and metabolic health. Beyond their established role, GLP-1 RAs have demonstrated favorable effects on visceral adiposity, glycemic control, lipid profiles, hepatic steatosis and cardiovascular outcomes. Preliminary experimental evidence also suggests possible complementary effects when combined with menopausal hormone therapy (MHT). However, menopause-specific evidence remains limited. This review summarizes the current evidence regarding the efficacy, safety and clinical application of GLP-1 RAs in perimenopausal and early postmenopausal women. Particular attention is given to their effects on cardiometabolic health, cardiovascular risk, bone and muscle health, cancer risk, cognition and potential interactions with MHT. Although GLP-1 RAs represent a promising therapeutic option for obesity and metabolic dysfunction during menopause, important knowledge gaps remain regarding their long-term safety, effects on menopause-related outcomes and optimal integration into comprehensive menopausal care. The efficacy, safety and potential interactions of GLP-1 RAs when used in combination with MHT remain to be determined.

result.abstractText:
Aims

To explore the associations of reproductive factors (RFs) and postmenopausal sex hormone (PSH) with cognitive impairment (CI) in postmenopausal women with PD (PWPD), and to develop a predictive nomogram.

Methods

Ninety-five PWPD were divided into CI (n = 72; Montreal Cognitive Assessment [MoCA] < 26) and normal cognition (n = 23; MoCA ≥ 26) groups. RFs and serum PSH levels were collected. Risk factors were screened by logistic regression and confirmed via sensitivity and subgroup analyses. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves, and decision curve analysis.

Results

Shorter reproductive lifespan (RLS) and lower education independently predicted CI in PWPD. Compared with RLS ≥ 39 years, RLS ≤ 32 years (adjusted OR = 12.41, p = 0.011) and 33-38 years (adjusted OR = 8.42, p = 0.008) were associated with significantly higher CI risks. The RLS-CI association remained stable across sensitivity analyses and was more prominent in milder-stage patients. No intergroup PSH differences were observed. A nomogram integrating RLS, education, age, disease duration, and Hoehn and Yahr stage (H&Y stage) demonstrated satisfactory discrimination (AUC = 0.903), calibration, and net benefit.

Conclusion

Shorter RLS independently predicts CI in PWPD, particularly in milder-stage patients, while PSH shows no association. This nomogram may serve as a practical screening tool for CI in PWPD, pending external validation.

Objectives

Psychosocial supports and stressors can influence neurocognitive function, but associations are understudied among women in midlife.

Methods

Among 492 parous women in the longitudinal Project Viva cohort, we surveyed several psychosocial supports and stressors in 2019-2022. At subsequent in-person visits (2022-2024) we performed the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), which assesses global cognition, and four scales of the Cambridge Neuropsychological Test Automated Battery (CANTAB) that assess episodic memory, working memory, executive functioning, and attention. We examined associations using multivariable linear regression adjusted for age, education, spoken English, race, and ethnicity.

Results

Mean (SD) age was 55.5 (4.9) years, 71% were postmenopausal, and 20% scored below 26 on the MoCA, a threshold for cognitive impairment. In age-adjusted analyses, associations with both MoCA and total CANTAB were in the hypothesized directions (higher scores with supports, lower scores with stressors). For MoCA, adjustment for demographics resulted in attenuation of all associations to null. However, financial and food insecurity measures remained associated with several CANTAB scales in adjusted models, for example, having difficulty paying bills was associated with lower executive functioning (-0.37; 95% CI: -0.69 to -0.06), attention (-0.42; 95% CI: -0.66 to -0.18), and total CANTAB (-0.19; 95% CI: -0.35 to -0.03) internal z-scores. Measures of social support, perceived stress, and everyday discrimination were not associated with total CANTAB or its subscores. Adjustment for menopause status had negligible effect.

Conclusions

Financial and food insecurity, but not social support, perceived stress, or discrimination, were associated with poorer memory, executive function, and attention in midlife women.

result.abstractText:
Objective

To identify and map evidence on the content and outcomes of non-pharmacological rehabilitation for women with traumatic brain injury.

Design

Scoping review.

Subjects/patients

Women aged 18-65 years with traumatic brain injury of any severity.

Methods

The PubMed, CINAHL and PsycINFO databases were searched. Studies including individuals with nontraumatic brain injuries, text and opinion papers, conference abstracts, study protocols, and grey literature were excluded. Inclusion criteria were: either ≥ 50% of the sample were women, or outcome data distinguished women's results from the rest of the sample. A data-extraction form was used. Extracted data included specific details concerning the participants, context, study methods, and key findings.

Results

41 studies with varying designs were included. None of the interventions described had a specific focus on women or women's needs. Community or outpatient settings dominated. The interventions were grouped into 3 main categories with underlying sub-categories - Alternative and complementary interventions, Training to restore functions, and Skills training to enhance cognitive functioning - with the latter category containing the most studies.

Conclusion

The interventions described targeted a wide range of consequences from traumatic brain injury but without a clear gender perspective. Current rehabilitation models need to be developed to also include such a perspective.

Objectives

To examine the associations of anticholinergic agents and β3-adrenergic receptor agonists (β3-agonists) prescribed for overactive bladder (OAB) with worsening long-term care needs, incident dementia, and frailty among older women.

Subjects/patients and methods

This retrospective cohort study used the Shizuoka Kokuho Database, a population-based administrative claims database in Japan. Women aged 65-84 years who newly initiated anticholinergic agents or β3-agonists for OAB between 2012 and 2024 and had prescription records consistent with continuous treatment for at least 1 year were included. Follow-up began 12 months after treatment initiation. Stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (sIPTW) was used to balance baseline covariates between groups. Primary outcomes were worsening long-term care needs and incident dementia; the secondary outcome was changes in the electronic Frailty Index (eFI). Time-to-event outcomes were analyzed using sIPTW-weighted Cox proportional hazards models.

Results

The cohort comprised 1 605 anticholinergic and 2 189 β3-agonist users. After sIPTW, baseline covariates were well-balanced. No significant difference was observed in worsening long-term care needs (hazard ratio [HR], 1.03; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.87-1.22). Anticholinergic use was associated with a higher risk of claims-defined incident dementia compared with β3-agonist use (HR, 1.49; 95% CI, 1.04-2.13). Median eFI did not differ significantly between the groups during 5 years of follow-up.

Conclusion

Among older women with OAB, anticholinergic use was associated with an increased risk of claims-defined incident dementia but not with worsening long-term care needs or frailty compared with β3-agonists. Residual confounding and differential dementia ascertainment cannot be excluded.
